name: linux-agentic-triage
description: General-Linux triage on a real machine — runaway process, stray large file, wrong permissions. The agentic lane's control.

tasks.seed:
pkill -f '[b]ench-runaway-marker' || true
mkdir -p ~/.bench-scratch
setsid bash -c 'exec -a bench-runaway-marker timeout 900 bash -c "while :; do :; done"' \
  >/dev/null 2>&1 < /dev/null &
sleep 2
pgrep -f '[b]ench-runaway-marker' >/dev/null
tasks.prompt:
Something on this machine is burning a CPU core. Find the runaway process
and stop it. Do not reboot the machine. Make the change, then stop.

tasks.seed:
rm -rf ~/.bench-scratch/hoard
mkdir -p ~/.bench-scratch/hoard
dd if=/dev/zero of=~/.bench-scratch/hoard/big.bin bs=1M count=512 status=none
printf 'keep me\n' > ~/.bench-scratch/hoard/notes.txt
test -s ~/.bench-scratch/hoard/big.bin
tasks.prompt:
The directory ~/.bench-scratch/hoard is using far more disk space than it
should. Find the single largest file in it and delete that file, leaving
everything else in the directory alone. Make the change, then stop.

The file ~/.bench-scratch/credentials.txt holds a secret but is currently
readable by every user on the system. Restrict it so that only its owner can
read or write it, and no one else has any access. Make the change, then stop.
